verdict: Yes for the merge itself, with one reservation that the owner has to decide before it goes on the main branch. Commit e3dbc812d on branch stage1c-m2-merged holds milestone M2 (simple probing on equations, R1) and the three commits of the parallel-row repair, both whole: 504 tests pass in both builds, all 115 wrong engines apply and are caught, 168 million release and 84 million assertion campaign models are clean, the check tool has no failed verdict on the 17 and the 240 local dumps, both identity statements hold, and no instance is larger than before in default or primal-only mode. The reservation: the parallel-row repair that the merge brings in has three wrong results that its author's report does not name. Its attacker found them; his report is missing (attack and triage are null in my task) and his repair lies uncommitted in the worktree /Users/acoerduek/Documents/workspace/cuopt/.claude/worktrees/wf_f36af1da-339-3. I reproduced the three on the merged engine and did not repair them, because that is the repair's own review and not this step. Two feasible models of three parallel rows are reported infeasible (the base engine returns points that are off by 1.6e-2 and 1.1e-6 on them), and one infeasible model is reduced to a point that is off by 1.35e-6 (the base engine reports it infeasible). No campaign model, none of the 240 and none of the 17 local dumps shows them, because the generator cannot draw them. If no known new wrong result may enter the branch, merge edd147a7e (M2 alone, unchanged by me) and hold the repair until its attack is finished. The reviews of M2 (validity, worth) are missing as well, so what stands for M2 beyond its author's report is my verification of the merged tree.

assumptions.title: Simple probing (R1): limit on the scale of an alias
assumptions.statement: A row is left when the range upper - lower of one of its other columns is above 1e6; the range is the scale of the alias and multiplies the coefficients of the column into the rows of the binary.
assumptions.alternatives: Any value from 1 up; inf for no limit.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, merged engine: with 1 and with inf every instance has the hash of the default run, and no visit is left for the limit. Campaign, 168 million release models: 84,912 visits left for it.

assumptions.title: Simple probing (R1): tolerance of the balance test
assumptions.statement: A row is visited only when its two activities lie equally far from its side within one feasibility tolerance, less the two error bounds. That is stricter than the two forcing tests by themselves, which allow two tolerances.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, merged engine: with 2 and with 0 every instance has the hash of the default run.

assumptions.title: Simple probing (R1): the binary and its neighbours must have the bounds 0 and 1
assumptions.statement: The binary, and every other integer column of the row whose bounds are one apart, must have the bounds 0 and 1 exactly. The design asks for upper - lower == 1 only. The author's reason: only then is the offset of every alias a bound of its own column whichever root the forest picks.
assumptions.alternatives: Bounds one apart at any place, as the design writes it.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, merged engine: no visit is left for it. Campaign, 168 million release models: 531,733 visits left for it.

assumptions.title: Simple probing (R1): a continuous column whose range is of rounding size is left
assumptions.statement: A row is left when the rounding of the two bounds of a continuous column is above tol.zero times its range, or when the slack of the forcing tests is above tol.zero times the smallest term range of a continuous column. This is the author's repair of the wrong reduction that his campaign found; the two thresholds are chosen by argument.
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own; tolerances_t::zero = 1e-9 (gpu_presolve/include/gprs/numerics.hpp:25)
assumptions.alternatives: Another factor than tol.zero; a test on the term range alone.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, merged engine: no visit is left for it. Campaign: 28 visits in 168 million release models and 10 in 84 million assertion models, no failure.

assumptions.title: Simple probing (R1): size of an offset
assumptions.statement: A row is left when max(|lower|, |upper|) of a column times its largest coefficient is above feasibility / side_error (1e8), or when a finite side of a row of the column is not readable. The call then reports limited, because the test reads rows that change without an event of the visited row, so the presolve does not end at a fixed point.
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own; tolerances_t::side_error = 1e-14 and feasibility = 1e-6 (gpu_presolve/include/gprs/numerics.hpp:23, 36)
assumptions.alternatives: No test, as the doubleton equations have none; a limit of its own.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, merged engine: no visit is left for it and no fixed-point flag is lost. Campaign, 168 million release models: 1,912 visits left for it.

assumptions.title: Simple probing (R1): which rows are visited
assumptions.statement: Only an equation with three or more free entries, a readable side and two finite activities is visited, and only explicit bounds of the columns are read (no implied bound).
assumptions.alternatives: Inequalities (not in the design); implied bounds.

assumptions.title: Simple probing (R1): the forcing test
assumptions.statement: The other entries must be forcing at both values of the binary's term by the test that the forcing row uses: a gap of zero within feasibility times min|a| / max(1, max|a|), with 8 rounding units allowed for a continuous column.
assumptions.where: gpu_presolve/src/forcing.hpp:25 and the function forcing below it; gpu_presolve/src/rules_simple_probing.cpp:181-184, 277-278
assumptions.switch: no switch (forcing_rounding_units = 8 is a named constant shared with the forcing row)
assumptions.alternatives: A tolerance of its own for the rule.

assumptions.title: Simple probing (R1): order of the binaries and one batch per call
assumptions.statement: The columns that can be the binary are tried in increasing index and the first that passes is taken. A call collects one batch from one state; a row whose columns the batch connects already waits for the next call. A row is deleted only when all its edges became maps.
assumptions.alternatives: Largest step first; apply after every row.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, merged engine: 952 visits on 2 instances were left because two columns were connected, and all 24,819 rows of the batches were deleted, none left with a cut edge.

assumptions.title: Simple probing (R1): place in the round, family switch and budget
assumptions.statement: The family runs first of the column rules, after the doubleton equations, with the budget of 4 passes, 2 stall passes and a floor of 100,000 work units. The budget is tested between two rows only and never while a batch is applied.
assumptions.alternatives: Another place in the round; another budget.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, merged engine: with the family off the run equals that of the repair commit on every instance; with it on 8 instances are smaller and none larger. Other places or budgets not measured.

assumptions.title: Parallel rows: which row of a pair is kept
assumptions.statement: Of two parallel rows without singleton columns the one with the larger coefficients is kept, the size read from the coefficient of the smallest core column, and the smaller index between rows of one size. The base kept the smaller index whatever the sizes.
assumptions.alternatives: Smaller index (the base); the row with the smaller sides.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, merged engine: with the option off the sizes are equal on all 240 and the hash differs on momentum1 and rocII-5-11. With propagation off the larger kept row costs rocII-5-11 376 rows, 169 columns and 1,959 nonzeros. The three wrong results named above come with the larger kept row.

assumptions.title: Parallel rows: limit on rows that are no exact multiples
assumptions.statement: Rows that are parallel within tol.zero and not exactly are merged, and an equation is subtracted from such a row, only when they differ by at most 0.1 of the feasibility tolerance over the explicit bounds of their columns, in the units of the removed row. A pair that fails reports limited.
assumptions.alternatives: inf for no limit; 0 for exact multiples only; a limit in the units of the kept row as well, which the attacker's unfinished repair adds.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, merged engine: with inf and with 0 every instance has the hash of the default run. The first wrong result above passes this limit and is wrong in the units of the kept row.

assumptions.title: Parallel rows: unit of the crossing test
assumptions.statement: Sides that cross are measured in the units of the removed row (crossing times |ratio|): infeasible above the feasibility tolerance, a merge with the new side at the opposite side of the kept row within it, and no merge when the rounding of the image and the drift do not place it on one side.
assumptions.alternatives: Units of the kept row; exact arithmetic; a sum over the merges of one row, which the attacker's unfinished repair adds.
assumptions.measured: Not measured on instances. The third wrong result above is two such merges in a row.

assumptions.title: Parallel rows: image of a side and its rounding
assumptions.statement: The image of a side is exact wherever it is a double. A rounded image is allowed 8 rounding units, is used only when the side of the removed row less its fixed terms is at most 1e8 (feasibility / side_error), and a side below 2^-960 leaves the pair alone. A rounded image becomes a side of the kept row as it is.
assumptions.switch: no switch (two named constants; the size limit follows tolerances_t::side_error and feasibility)
assumptions.alternatives: Another allowance; refusing a rounded image as a side of the kept row when its rounding is above a share of the tolerance in that row's units, which the attacker's unfinished repair adds.
assumptions.measured: Not measured on instances. The second wrong result above is a rounded image taken as a side.

assumptions.title: Parallel rows: fixed terms of the kept row and the limited flag
assumptions.statement: A pair is left when the kept (larger) row holds fixed terms above 1e8. Refusals that read column bounds or the fixed terms of the kept row report limited, so the presolve then does not end at a fixed point.
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own (tolerances_t::side_error, feasibility)
assumptions.alternatives: Asking the smaller row, as the base did.
assumptions.measured: 240 and 17 local dumps, merged engine, default and primal-only: no fixed-point flag is lost against the engine before, and the sizes equal those of the M2 commit on every instance.

assumptions.title: Generator and campaign of the two works (tests only)
assumptions.statement: Probing rows are drawn only with p_probing_row > 0 (--probing: 0.7, up to 3 rows); probing_wide is kept out of campaigns. Parallel rows of very different scale are drawn only with p_parallel_scale > 0 (profile parallel_scale: 0.8, factors up to 2^20). The profile scale_pair ignores every profile option and is judged by the side points alone; the side points run on no other profile.
assumptions.switch: generator_options_t::p_probing_row = 0, max_probing_rows = 2, probing_wide = false, p_parallel_scale = 0, max_parallel_scale_exp2 = 20; gprs_fuzz --probing, --probing-wide, --profile <name>
assumptions.alternatives: Side points on every profile; a generator of three parallel rows with sides that cross within the tolerance, of rows that are no exact multiples at a ratio far from 1, and of decimal sides near 1e10.
assumptions.measured: Campaign of this step: 168 million release and 84 million assertion models, clean. The three wrong results of the repair are outside what these knobs draw.

assumptions.title: The merge itself
assumptions.statement: The merge chooses no default, limit, tolerance or order that decides a reduction. Where both works appended to a list, the entries of M2 stand before those of the repair.
assumptions.measured: Identity runs: the merged engine with simple probing off equals the repair commit on the 240 and the 17 local dumps and on 2.6 million random models per build.
